description:
The Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to provide financial assistance to construction workers during the festive season of Diwali. 

This scheme was introduced under the aegis of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and is specifically aimed at benefiting the members of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The scheme was officially launched on October 15, 2021. 

The primary objective of the Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme is to provide a monetary benefit to construction workers to help them celebrate the festival of lights with dignity and joy. 

The government aims to distribute financial assistance to approximately 2.5 million construction workers across India. 

The specific target is to provide a one-time financial assistance of ₹5,000 to each eligible construction worker. 

This assistance is intended to alleviate the financial burden that may arise during the festive season. 

The scheme is particularly significant as it recognizes the contributions of construction workers who often work in challenging conditions and may not have substantial savings. 

To be eligible for the Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme, applicants must be registered members of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The minimum age requirement for eligibility is 18 years. 

There is no upper age limit specified for eligibility under this scheme. 

Additionally, applicants must have been registered with the welfare board for at least six months prior to the application date. 

The income criteria for eligibility are not strictly defined in terms of a maximum income limit. 

However, it is generally expected that applicants should be engaged in construction work as their primary source of income. 

The application process for the Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme is straightforward and designed to facilitate easy access for construction workers. 

Interested applicants must visit the official website of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

They are required to fill out an online application form specifically designated for the Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme. 

The application form requires basic personal details such as name, age, address, and registration number with the welfare board. 

Applicants must also provide proof of their identity and registration with the board. 

Documents required for the application include a copy of the registration certificate as a construction worker, an identity proof such as an Aadhar card or voter ID, and a recent passport-sized photograph. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities of the welfare board. 

The disbursement of the financial assistance is typically processed within a month of the application submission. 

The scheme is designed to ensure that the funds are transferred directly to the bank accounts of the eligible construction workers. 

The financial assistance is disbursed annually during the Diwali festival season. 

In 2021, the disbursement was made on November 1, just ahead of the Diwali celebrations. 

The implementing authority for the Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme is the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India. 

The Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board operates under this ministry and is responsible for the execution of the scheme. 

Each state has its own Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board which administers the scheme at the state level. 

For any queries or assistance, construction workers can contact the local office of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The contact details for these offices can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

The Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme is part of a broader effort by the Indian government to support marginalized and economically disadvantaged groups during festive seasons. 

The scheme is expected to boost the morale of construction workers and their families by providing them with financial support during a time of celebration. 

In the context of rising costs of living and inflation, this financial assistance is particularly timely and relevant. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹1,250 crores for the implementation of this scheme in the current fiscal year. 

This allocation reflects the government's commitment to the welfare of construction workers and their families. 

The scheme is also seen as a way to promote social inclusion and ensure that all segments of society can partake in the festive celebrations. 

The Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders, including labor unions and worker advocacy groups. 

These groups have emphasized the importance of such initiatives in recognizing the hard work of construction workers. 

As of October 2023, the scheme continues to be operational and is expected to be a recurring initiative every year during the Diwali festival. 

The government is also exploring ways to enhance the scheme in future years based on feedback from beneficiaries. 

This could include increasing the financial assistance amount or expanding eligibility criteria to include more workers. 

The Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme is a testament to the Indian government's efforts to uplift the working class and provide them with necessary support during important cultural events. 

It serves as a reminder of the importance of social welfare schemes in promoting economic stability and social equity. 

The scheme not only provides financial aid but also fosters a sense of community and belonging among construction workers. 

The government encourages all eligible construction workers to take advantage of this scheme and ensure their participation. 

By doing so, they can enjoy the festive season without the added stress of financial constraints. 

The Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme is one of many initiatives aimed at improving the lives of workers in India. 

It highlights the government's recognition of the vital role that construction workers play in the nation's economy. 

Overall, the scheme represents a significant step towards enhancing the welfare of construction workers during one of the most celebrated festivals in India.
